fields.statement: QA at b92987bf with a built binary (go build -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza), by hand: in a fresh scratch git repo with its own HOME and every RHIZA_* variable unset, typed each docs/quickstart.md bash block in order (git init, init, change new, apply --dry-run, apply intent.json, propose, accept, land, show/why/slice export-csv, tree, render, check, git add/commit). Every command exited 0; show listed decided-by csv-streaming, why showed the quote and the landed change set, tree showed reports > export-csv, render wrote 5 files, check printed ok, and git status was clean after the commit. go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/quickstart passes, and fails (unknown command treee, quickstart.txtar:8) after I changed the doc's rhiza tree to rhiza treee, so doc drift is caught.

QA at b92987bf: go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/doclinks/... passes over the real README.md and docs/. With README's quickstart link changed to docs/quickstart-nope.md it fails with README.md:23 docs/quickstart-nope.md does not exist; with the quickstart's ../README.md#install changed to #installing it fails with docs/quickstart.md:3 no heading #installing in README.md. Both edits reverted afterwards.

QA at b92987bf: read README.md. It covers what and why, install via go install github.com/dphaener/rhiza/cmd/rhiza@latest (matches go.mod's module and go 1.25) or release binaries for linux/darwin amd64/arm64 with checksums.txt (matches .goreleaser.yaml), a link to docs/quickstart.md, a note that the concepts, agents and reference pages are still to come, and an MIT LICENSE file. The built binary's version, --help, guide and describe commands that it points to all run. Its relative links resolve (doclinks test). The owner still has to sign off.
